title: Integrate planned-game repository proposals and Codex handoff
summary: Turn a ratified game charter and Board into a reviewable repository scaffold proposal, implementation package, and later reconciliation without creating a remote automatically.
acceptance_criteria: Turn a ratified game charter and Board into a reviewable repository scaffold proposal, implementation package, and later reconciliation without creating a remote automatically.
Keep repository-owned product and domain truth outside HumbleControl.
Use repository-qualified identities for applications, tickets, capabilities, fixtures, releases, and evidence.
Distinguish planned, current, stale, blocked, unavailable, not-run, unknown, and passed states.
Define versioning, migration, compatibility, and deprecation from the first schema version.
Document the exact boundary between shared portfolio infrastructure and game-owned behavior.
Support Sudoku and Kakuro as real fixtures before claiming generality.
Support planning-only future repositories without pretending they exist or are authorized.
Add deterministic validation for malformed, old, new, missing, and conflicting inputs.
Preserve historical decisions through supersession instead of rewriting them.
Expose readable human output and a machine-readable contract.
Provide accessibility and localization for every user-facing control or report.
Measure performance on the current portfolio fixture before enforcing a budget.
Do not grant permissions or execute repository creation merely because a plan exists.
Record all unavailable external, device, App Store, or user-research evidence honestly.
Integrate with existing ticket, assurance, performance, agent, release, and lifecycle contracts.
Pass focused tests, repository contract validation, ticket validation, and diff hygiene.

trigger.source_ref: Jan requested Wave 12, a deep reanalysis of every prior ticket, an urgent Kakuro board fix, and gated planning for new game repositories after Sudoku reaches 100% completion.

agent_notes: Non-scope: do not release, deploy, create paid products, enable external ads, create GitHub repositories, migrate data, or start new game implementation without the explicit gate.
Alternative considered and rejected: cloning HumbleSudoku into many repositories before Sudoku is complete would multiply defects, warnings, and product debt.
Every completed implementation must leave zero app-owned warnings.
